biography.plain_text: The Oneglia family is the founding family behind O&G Industries, a fourth-generation construction group based in Torrington, Connecticut. Established by Andrew Oneglia and Flaviano Gervasini in 1923, the company combines building and heavy-civil contracting. Its operations include quarries, asphalt and concrete plants, masonry products and a large equipment fleet serving the northeastern United States.

confidence.reason: O&G's official history establishes the founders, date, location, fourth-generation family ownership, construction divisions, materials network and equipment platform. Independent reporting corroborates the family continuity and regional construction identity.

long_biography.plain_text:
The enterprise began with two dump trucks and a steamroller, hauling sand and stone before winning road-building work. After co-founder Flaviano Gervasini died in an accident, Andrew Oneglia continued with members of both families. The company added ready-mix concrete, quarries and masonry supplies, creating a vertically integrated platform around the materials its projects consumed.

Successive Oneglia generations expanded O&G into building construction, heavy civil engineering, construction management and materials production. Family owners remain active in daily operations, while fourth-generation executives now develop business, lead operating divisions and advance environmental improvements. The result is a century-spanning family enterprise whose contracting work is supported by its own plants, quarries, equipment fleet and repair facilities.
